findings.claim: Watch.__init__ materializes every parsed Entry with list(entries(...)) before extracting startup fingerprints. Evicted cache entries therefore remain owned by the list, making startup memory O(total closed-record payload) rather than the contracted per-job traversal. A synthetic store of 48 records carrying 1 MiB notes peaked at 49.5 MiB while the bounded cache retained 15.1 MiB; sufficiently large stores can terminate the watcher before its armed line.
findings.reproduce: Create 48 closed record copies with 1 MiB envelope notes, start Watch under tracemalloc, and compare peak memory with closed_cache.retained_upper_bound; measured 49.5 MiB peak versus 15.1 MiB retained at e7315a15. The source uses initial = list(entries(...)); the contract requires enumeration and parsing per job rather than accumulation in one list.

findings.claim: error_fingerprint calls os.lstat on the compound path in/plan.md relative to the job fd. lstat refuses only the final component, so a symlinked job/in is traversed and metadata outside the job directory enters the fingerprint, contrary to the contract's intermediate-symlink boundary. External file changes can consequently drive watchdog deviation and error notifications.
findings.reproduce: Plant job/record.json as a symlink to force an unreadable entry and job/in as a symlink to an external directory. Construct Watch, rewrite external/plan.md, and run one tick; at e7315a15 the fingerprint changes and stdout emits both deviation unavailable and watchdog error: InputUnavailable.
